pr_title: HTTP SD: Allow charset in content type
pr_body:
<!--

    - Performance improvements would need a benchmark test to prove it.

    - All comments should start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
 -->

This PR replaces the `Content-Type` header check, which only allows `application/json`, with a regex that allows multiple (valid) combinations and formats of `application/json; charset=utf-8`.

(credit to @roidelapluie for the regex)

Fixes #8971
pr_comments: I noticed that this regex still allows an infinite number of spaces between `application/json` and `charset=utf-8` (example: application/json;  charset=utf-8). I don't think the standard explicitly disallows it, but should we?
Wait . Did I really forget to push my http_test.go with my tests? 😅
Ya know, I do remember finding it weird that there were none

issue_context.title: HTTP SD: allow charset in content type
issue_context.body:
Currently the HTTP SD only allows application/json, exactly.

Since content type can also contain the charset : application/json;charset=utf8,
we could support it as well.

Note: only utf-8 is allowed.

Questions:

Which kind of spaces are allowed? Do we need regexes? Which other options could be set? Is there a way to decode that header in the std lib?
comments:
According to RFC, the following are equivalent:

     text/html;charset=utf-8
     text/html;charset=UTF-8
     Text/HTML;Charset="utf-8"
     text/html; charset="utf-8"


I guess that will be a lot of fun to parse.

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7231#section-3.1.1.1

So we'll need to support:

```
 application/json;charset=utf-8
 application/json;charset=UTF-8
 Application/JSON;Charset="utf-8"
 application/jsonl; charset="utf-8"
```

and so on.

Is any random combination of capital and lowercase letters allowed?

why jsonl;? typo?

Yes it is case insensitive as I understand it. just call .ToLower i guess.

Whoops typo. I can work on this.

Maybe just a regex idk
